title: VPC image provenance and zero-egress upgrade contract
creator: Maya Kapoor
description: Define unambiguous requirements and acceptance criteria for performing Private/VPC upgrades with zero or minimal egress by validating image provenance and a deterministic bootstrapping handshake. This ticket captures product decisions for upgrade workflows in highly restricted networks (air-gapped or egress-locked), clarifies scope, and lists verification steps for engineering and SRE teams.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated environments require upgrades and node provisioning without outbound network access. Current upgrade designs assume an online control plane or temporary egress windows. We need a contract that codifies how images, artifacts, and manifests are delivered, validated, and applied in zero-egress scenarios while minimizing operator intervention and preserving rollbacks and auditability.
goals: Define an image provenance contract (signatures, checksums, and metadata) that can be validated entirely offline
Specify an upgrade handshake protocol that works with no outbound egress (e.g., signed bundles, local mirrors, and pre-seeded root-of-trust)
Produce acceptance criteria and test vectors for air-gapped upgrade verification
Document operational playbook for restricted-network upgrades including failure recovery paths and rollback criteria
non_goals: Designing a full package distribution system (we will rely on existing artifact mirrors or customer-provided registry)
Implementing cryptographic tooling (engineering will choose libs, this ticket defines required properties)
Guaranteeing zero-downtime for all cluster sizes (we will define SLOs and recommended maintenance windows)
scope: Covers: image signing requirements, bundle formats for offline transfer, local mirror validation checks, upgrade orchestration contract (what the control plane expects when no egress), preflight checks, post-upgrade verification, and audit logging. Excludes: full implementation details and UI changes; those will be separate ENG/DES tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact bundle format is specified: tar.gz with manifest.json, images, checksums, and a detached signature file
Manifest schema defined and includes fields for version, image digests, build metadata, and signing key IDs
Signing model documented: support for HSM/KMS-backed signing, root-of-trust bootstrap procedure, and key rotation guidance
Offline validation flow documented: given a bundle placed on a node, the node can validate signatures and checksums without contacting external servers
Upgrade handshake contract specified: control plane accepts a signed upgrade intent file and verifies local artifacts before applying
Rollback criteria enumerated: explicit verification failure states result in automatic abort and clear operator-facing diagnostics
End-to-end acceptance test vectors provided: three sample bundles (clean, tampered checksum, expired signature) and expected validation outcomes
Operational playbook produced: step-by-step instructions for performing an upgrade with only removable media or internal registries, including post-upgrade verification commands
Audit log spec included: events for bundle ingestion, validation results, upgrade start, upgrade completion, and rollback with timestamps and responsible principal
rollout_plan: Draft spec reviewed with Engineering and Security (week 1)
Iterate spec with Engineering implementation constraints (week 2)
Create ENG tickets for bundle parser, signature verifier, and offline preflight checks (week 3)
Produce test bundles and run in-house air-gapped lab to validate criteria (week 4)
Ship v1 contract doc and playbook; collect customer feedback from two beta customers (week 5-6)
risks: Customers may have incompatible internal registry formats or internal policies that prevent straightforward mirror usage
Key management complexity: customers may be unwilling to expose private signing keys to Redwood; we must support BYO-keys and multiple trust models
Operational complexity of rollback in severely restricted networks could require manual intervention that lengthens outages
Edge cases around large model/artifact sizes and removable-media transfer rates could make upgrades time-consuming
open_questions: What minimum cryptographic primitives are required (e.g., RSA-4096 vs ECDSA) or do we accept multiple algorithms?
Should we mandate a specific bundle layout or allow multiple versions with a compatibility shim?
How should we represent provenance metadata to support automated policy checks (e.g., SBOM-like fields)?
Do we require a specific format for operator-facing diagnostics to simplify SRE runbooks?
stakeholders: Engineering: Ethan Rivera (assignee), Priya Singh (runtime lead)
notes: Leverage existing image signing patterns (cosign/sigstore) but do not hard-bind to specific OSS projects in the spec; require interoperable outputs
Consider small, machine-readable test vectors (50–200KB) so labs can run faster
Audit events must be exportable to customer SIEMs via existing logging integrations
